$comment: Every page published outside this repository, and what it asserts. Created 2026-09-02 after a shared page was found stating 786 tokens against a repo holding 829 — stale for four days with nothing able to notice, because only 1 of 9 artifact manifests declared a surface.ref and four published pages had no registered artifact at all (C-028). Not everything published belongs in artifacts/ — a runbook is not a design deliverable — but everything published that makes CLAIMS about this system has to be trackable, or the claim drifts in someone else's hands.
the_rule: A page listed here declares `documents` — the release, count, or state its content is true of. When the repository moves past that, the page is stale BY DEFINITION and does not need a human to notice. `documents: null` means the page makes no claim that can go stale, and must say why.

surfaces.title: CoForge Visual Foundations
surfaces.note: A measurement of coforge.com, hashed in ART-005's manifest, PLUS a section describing our own token layer. That second part is what goes stale — and it appears nowhere in the registered 124-line payload, so the published surface asserts more than the artifact backs. Corrected 2026-09-02; the site measurements were deliberately left untouched.

surfaces.title: Body Face Bake-off
surfaces.note: A typeface comparison measured 2026-08-27. Records a decision and the measurements behind it; both are historical and neither tracks repository state. OQ-2 closed on it. Nothing here can go stale.

surfaces.title: CoForge Agentic Design
surfaces.note: The system map, published 2026-08-28 and untouched since. UNVERIFIED and very likely the stalest surface we have: since that date tokens moved 786 -> 829 and 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0, three artifacts were added, corrections went 10 -> 28, and the whole validation layer landed. It has no registered artifact, so nothing anchors what it claims. Needs reading before it is trusted or shared.

surfaces.title: CoForge System Board
surfaces.note: A live status board of governance, foundations and blockers. Derived entirely from sources of truth and regenerable, so it does not need to be an artifact — but every figure on it is a claim about repository state, which makes it the fastest-staling page here.

surfaces.title: MCP Reset Runbook
surfaces.note: Operational instructions for restoring the Figma bridge. Describes tooling outside this repository, not repository state, so no version anchors it. Goes stale when the tooling changes, which no check here can observe — stated rather than pretended otherwise.

surfaces.title: Figma <-> Claude Bridge
surfaces.note: Setup notes for the local bridge, published 2026-08-24 — the oldest surface. Same class as the runbook: external tooling, unanchored, unobservable from here.

known_limits.shared_flag: `shared` is null where this session could not observe it. The share state lives in the artifact's own menu, not in any API reachable from here, so it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed. It matters: a shared page puts wrong figures in someone else's hands, and a viewer may be pinned to a version older than the live one.
known_limits.no_content_check: Nothing here reads the published HTML. A check can compare `documents` against the repository and say a page is stale; it cannot confirm a page is CORRECT. Those are different claims and only the first is automatable from inside CI.
